chunks: Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abā Ibrāhīm عليه السلام about a flint, a reed, and a piece of wood with which a person may slaughter if he does not find a knife. He said: "If it severs the veins, then there is no harm in that."

key_terms.الْأَوْدَاجَ: the neck veins required to be cut in slaughter
key_terms.الْقَصَبَةِ: a reed used as a cutting implement
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: flint or sharp stone used for cutting
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to slaughter an animal with something other than a knife in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning slaughter when a knife is unavailable. It indicates that the validity of slaughter depends on properly severing the veins, not strictly on the use of a knife itself.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4163 - Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as)) about using a flint, a reed, or a piece of wood to slaughter an animal if one does not have a knife.
Imam (as) said: "If it cuts the veins, then there is no harm in it."
